_doc: The Overboard rider HUD. One spec for the offline renders (tools/hud/render_hud.py) and the game HUD. Sizes are pixels at a 1080-pixel-high frame; scale them by frame height / 1080. Colours are sRGB hex with alpha 0..1. See docs/hud-spec.md.

torque.label: TORQUE
torque._doc: A centred bar: drive fills right of centre, braking left (both teal; the side and the sign carry the direction). Each end is the motor limit (Kt x i_limit), shown in the value as '+17 / 59 N.m'. Above near_limit_frac the fill turns amber. A torque at over_at_frac of the limit or beyond (a saturating controller never exceeds its limit) pins the fill at the end in red, with a red cap past the end and the value in red. top_px: the torque label's top, from the panel's inner top.

warning._doc: The same signal as the board's amber L5 LEDs: pulsed at pulse_hz on the pulsed bit, solid on the solid bit; the panel edge turns the chip colour (edge_px, edge_alpha). The handoff bit (Unreal owns the board) shows OVERBOARD in red, the edge red, and dims every value to muted at dim_alpha: the controller no longer rides.

margin._doc: 'margin' is the authority USED (controls track, control_core::AuthorityMargin): max(|filtered current| / limit, duty / 0.95, predicted grade current / limit); 1.0 = at the limit, and it can exceed 1. The warning (margin_level, with hysteresis) is pulsed on above 0.70 (off below 0.65) and solid on above 0.85 (off below 0.80). The HUD adds no element for it: from warm_from to warn_at the panel edge warms to amber, alpha lerping edge_alpha[0] to edge_alpha[1], clamped at warn_at, so the panel warms before the chip appears.

text._doc: Use U+2212 for the minus sign, so a sign is as wide as '+'.
